Playing Mario Party online (alpha)
==================================

Two to four players, each on their own computer with this same release, their own Mario Party (USA) ROM, the same
mods enabled and the same Board Movement and Map Scrolling settings. One player hosts; the others join.

1. Everyone: start MarioPartyRecompiled and pick your ROM with Load ROM the first time.
2. The host: choose Online Play in the launcher, set Online Play to Host and Players to how many play (you
   included), and press Start Online Game at the bottom.
3. Each other player: choose Online Play, set Online Play to Join, type the host's address and press Start Online
   Game. The host gives each player their number in the order they join.
4. The screen stays black while the game waits for every player (up to five minutes); then the game begins. Each
   player plays with their own first controller (or the keyboard).

To play alone again, set Online Play back to Off.

The host's address
------------------
The others must be able to reach UDP port 7845 on the host's computer:

- Easiest: everyone joins the same VPN (Radmin VPN, Tailscale or ZeroTier) and the host gives the address it shows.
- Over the internet without a VPN: forward UDP port 7845 on the host's router to the host's computer, and give the
  others the host's public address (a site such as whatismyip.com shows it).
- On the same home network: the host's local address (like 192.168.1.20).

Allow the program through the firewall if your computer asks.

What to expect
--------------
- Everyone plays from the host's save. A guest's own save isn't changed: its session saves to saves/netplay instead.
- The game measures the connection when the session starts and delays everyone's buttons just enough to cover it, so
  everyone sees the same game: a tenth of a second or so on a VPN.
- If something goes wrong (a player leaves, the copies differ, or the games ever play differently), each copy shows
  a message saying what happened and closes. A message about the game playing differently ("desynced") is a bug:
  each copy keeps a record of the session in its netplay/sessions folder (the message says where). Please send the
  newest folder from every player.

This is an alpha: there is no way yet to rejoin a session that ended, or to play without one player's port being
reachable.

host.bat / host.sh and join.bat / join.sh start a session from the command line instead, for testing.
